title: ‘Tangles’ Wins Grand Jury Prize at Animation Is Film Festival
description: “Tangles” won the Grand Jury Prize at the 9th annual Animation Is Film Festival. Directed by Leah Nelson, the 2-D animated film follows a family im
body:
“Tangles” won the Grand Jury Prize at the 9th annual Animation Is Film Festival. Directed by Leah Nelson, the 2-D animated film follows a family impacted by their mother’s battle with dementia.

	“We loved the fluid 2D animation which uses a stark monochrome framing to bring to life the personal story of a family impacted by the mother’s battle with dementia,” the features jury said. “We were especially impressed with how director Leah Nelson and her perfectly cast voice team were able to remain faithful to Sarah Leavitt’s graphic novel which tackles a serious, painful subject with great beauty, honesty, and a gentle touch and also offers a great flashback to 1990s-era San Francisco.”
	

	The Fumi Kitahara Special Jury Prize was awarded to “Iron Boy,” directed by Louis Clichy. The award was named in memory of publicist and champion of AIF’s mission Fumi Kitahara, who died in 2025. The film also won the Features Audience Award.


	The jury said: “’Iron Boy’ is pure beauty from the medium we all love. Louis Clichy’s ‘Iron Boy’ was an easy stand-out thanks to its beautifully crafted water-color-like and Chinese ink-brush style visuals and how it told a story inspired by the director’s own memories of growing up in rural France. We also admired the way Clichy conveyed a world of emotions with his impressionistic visuals as well as his depiction of a young boy’s personal struggles with a physical handicap and the heartfelt portrayal of a strained father-and-son relationship which avoids sentimentality and the pitfalls of a traditional comic-of-age story.”
	

	“Paper Trail,” directed by Don Hertzfeldt, won the Shorts Jury Grand Prize. The jury described the film as “unique and profoundly moving.”

	The Shorts Special Jury Prize went to “Please,” directed by Anna Mantzaris. The jury called it “a wonderfully made, funny, and tender film that captures the absurdity and very human longing for connection.”

	The 2026 feature competition lineup included “Cherry and Virgin” (Masanao Kawajiri), “Ghost — End of Night” (Shingo Natsume), “Iron Boy” (Louis Clichy), “Jim Queen” (Nicolas Athané and Marco Nguyen), “Julián” (Louise Bagnall), “O Filho Da Puta (Son of a Bitch)” (Otto Guerra, Érica Maradona, Tânia Anaya and Sávio Leite), “Tangles” (Leah Nelson), “The Violinist” (Ervin Han and Raúl García) and “Viva Carmen!” (Sébastien Laudenbach).

	The shorts in competition this year were “Acid City” (Jack Wedge and Will Freudenheim), “Because Today is a Saturday” (Alice Eça Guimarães), “Blessed” (Birute Sodeikaite), “Core Dump” (Alona Rodeh), “Daughters of the Late Colonel” (Elizabeth Hobbs), “God is Shy” (Jocelyn Charles), “Hag” (Anna Ginsburg), “It’s Not a Phase Mom” (Nataël Renault, Tianhui Song, Anna Watson, Léa Mau-Glicenstein, Riley Cords and Reni Park), “Living With a Visionary” (Stephen P. Neary), “Paper Trail” (Don Hertzfeldt), “Paradaïz” (Matea Radic), “Please” (Anna Mantzaris), “Saba” (Liron Topaz), “Tuna Tartare” (Lena Greene), “Ultra Strong” (Catherine Lepage), “What We Leave Behind” (Jean-Sébastien Hamel and Alexandra Myotte), “With Tapes and Toasts in the Car” (Kiana Naghshineh) and “Winter in March” (Natalia Mirzoyan).

	Over its four days, this year’s Animation Is Film Festival also included the first big-screen presentation of Dana Terrace’s “Knights of Guinevere,” a special screening of Laika’s “Wildwood” with director Travis Knight, a behind-the-scenes look at Disney’s “Hexed” and a presentation of work-in-progress “Clara and the Below,”

title: James Bond Final Screen Tests Are Happening This Week
description:
The crowning of the next James Bond is upon us.

	Final screen tests for Amazon MGM Studios‘ new 007 are set to happen in the next week, sources te
body:
The crowning of the next James Bond is upon us.

	Final screen tests for Amazon MGM Studios‘ new 007 are set to happen in the next week, sources tell Variety, beginning as early as Friday. Though who exactly will test is up in the air, Callum Turner and Jack Lowden appear to be in the mix.

	Reps for Turner, Lowden and Amazon MGM did not immediately respond to Variety‘s request for comment.


	Denis Villeneuve is set to direct the new Bond movie for Amazon MGM, with casting extraordinaire Nina Gold helming the audition process. A timeline has still not been given for when Amazon will officially name its next Bond, though the expectation is before the end of the year.
	

	Turner and Lowden have each had their moment in the Bond rumor mill, with Lowden recently moving to the forefront. Speculation reached fever pitch when the Scottish actor’s “Slow Horses” co-star Gary Oldman appeared to suggest that Lowden had made the shortlist. Lowden’s wife, Saoirse Ronan, later weighed in on the buzz, saying that it’s “not really a subject that’s coming up in our house.”

	British star Turner was a favorite for the spy earlier this year, with fans even fantasizing about the possibility of a Bond theme song by his wife Dua Lipa. While promoting arthouse film “Rosebush Pruning” at Berlin Film Festival in February, he was immediately asked about the rumors. “It’s very early for that question,” Turner said with a Bond-esque smirk. “I’m not going to comment on it.”

schema.headline: James Bond Final Screen Tests Are Happening This Week

title: ‘Elsinore’ to Receive Gotham Legacy Tribute in Honor of Ian Charleson (EXCLUSIVE)
description: The Gotham Film & Media Institute will recognize Focus Features’ “Elsinore” with a Gotham Legacy Tribute at the Gotham Film Awards on Nov. 30, hono
body:
The Gotham Film & Media Institute will recognize Focus Features’ “Elsinore” with a Gotham Legacy Tribute at the Gotham Film Awards on Nov. 30, honoring the film’s subject, actor Ian Charleson. 

	The tribute, which takes place at Cipriani Wall Street in New York, will honor the film and its star Andrew Scott, screenwriter Stephen Beresford and director Simon Stone for bringing the legacy of actor and advocate Charleson to new audiences. Charleson, who died in 1990, was the star of the Oscar-winning “Chariots of Fire.”
	

	“In his final months, Ian Charleson affirmed his talent, his determination, and what it means to be an actor,” said Jeffrey Sharp, Executive Director of The Gotham Film & Media Institute. “With Elsinore, Andrew Scott, Stephen Beresford, Simon Stone, and the entire production team have made a deeply moving film about a life devoted to performance and the community that supported him. We are delighted to celebrate Elsinore with the Gotham Legacy Tribute in recognition of the remarkable artist who inspired it.”


	“Elsinore” tells the story of the Scottish actor who received a devastating AIDS diagnosis at the same time as has the chance to take on the stage role of a lifetime in “Hamlet.” 

	“’Elsinore’ follows an actor at the height of his powers as he strives to command the stage, facing his own mortality with unflinching honesty, wit, and grace. His final performance becomes his greatest triumph, and a source of healing and inspiration for those around him,” the synopsis reads.

	In addition to Scott, “Elsinore” stars Olivia Colman, Billie Piper, Johnny Flynn, and Joe Locke. Colman plays Dr. Margaret Johnson, who treated Charleson and fellow gay men during the HIV epidemic, launching the first-ever dedicated HIV clinic. 
	

	“Elsinore” premiered at the Telluride Film Festival and went on to screen in the Special Presentations section at the Toronto International Film Festival, where it received the International People’s Choice Award. 

	It opens Nov. 20 in limited release and will expand over the Thanksgiving holiday and through December. “Elsinore” is produced by Studiocanal, LD Entertainment, Lucky Red and Magnolia Mae Films.

	Also at the Gotham Awards, “Michael” will receive the musical tribute, “La Bola Negra” will receive the Vanguard Tribute, Danny Boyle will receive the director tribute for “Ink” and Laika will receive the anniversary tribute. 

	Nominees for the 36th annual Gotham Film Awards will be announced on Oct. 27.

schema.headline: ‘Elsinore’ to Receive Gotham Legacy Tribute in Honor of Ian Charleson (EXCLUSIVE)

title: ‘Ali G: Who Iz I?’ Review: Sacha Baron Cohen Brings Back His Cretinous Fake OG Talk-Show Host, Only Now Ali G Is the Film’s ‘Political’ Subject. A Mistake, Innit?
description: Back in the day (as he would have put it), Ali G was my favorite Sacha Baron Cohen character. In the ’90s and early 2000s, there was something exqu
body:
Back in the day (as he would have put it), Ali G was my favorite Sacha Baron Cohen character. In the ’90s and early 2000s, there was something exquisitely daft about his track suit and do-rag wave cap, his “street” Cockney Jafaican patois, his insanely stunted worldview and brain-dead malapropisms (“Does you think that men should marry only one woman? Does you believe in mahogany?”), and in the more than slightly absurd Method commitment with which Baron Cohen immersed himself in the character.
	

	That said, Ali G would never have been more than an inspired sketch-comedy jape if it hadn’t been for all the politicians and public figures he interviewed — a parade of po-faced luminaries (Donald Trump, Ralph Nader, Buzz Aldrin, Christie Todd Whitman, Sam Donaldson), none of whom had any idea that they were being punked by a walking put-on. I’ll never forget the look on Pat Buchanan’s face when Ali G asked him if the U.S. had found “BLTs” in Iraq.


	But that was then. The joke of Ali G is that he was a maximally clueless white-bro poseur (a ripely legitimate topic for satire, since millions of white kids in Britain and the U.S. had mindlessly appropriated the style and attitude and language of hip-hop culture). But it’s a joke of its era that sits uncomfortably in the world of today. In 2026, the character of Ali G is so out of step that his presence now risks playing as an ironic nostalgic celebration of something it once – rightfully — skewered.

	“Ali G: Who Iz I?” is a movie that would like to do for Ali G what “Borat: Cultural Learnings of America for Make Benefit Glorious Nation of Kazakhstan” (2006) did for Borat and “Bruno” (2009) did for Bruno. Except that the new movie, which Baron Cohen directed himself, isn’t like those other films. They were guerrilla comedies, more documentary than not (pundits have been drawing comparison between “You Can See Everything” and “Borat”), in which the bulk of the comedy consisted of Borat or Bruno talking to ordinary Americans, who didn’t know they were being pranked, in a way that unmasked their idiocies and prejudices.
	

	There’s some of that in “Ali G: Who Iz I?,” but it’s all fairly minor and neutral. When Ali G’s romantic partner, Julie (Morgana Robinson), who’s pregnant with their child, attempts to purchase a mansion in Bel Air, the real-estate agent is the “straight” character (i.e., he’s not in on the joke), but he’s treated with total dignity. He’s just there to shuttle increasingly extreme messages back and forth between Ali G and Julie in what becomes a glorified comedy routine.

	There’s a scene with a liquor-store salesman who, likewise, isn’t the butt of the joke. And there are several scenes in which Baron Cohen, in character, talks to groups of people sitting in rows in meeting rooms — and what he says is so appalling that they walk out, or simply turn on him. These vérité extras aren’t there so that the film can ridicule or belittle them; they come off just fine. At the climax, a handful of right-wing would-be militia men are used as the butt of the joke in an elaborate sequence that’s all about foiling terrorists. (It’s also arrested in a “Jackass”/”Beavis and Butt-Head” way.) But it’s too little, too late. If the intent of “Ali G: Who Iz I?” is to reveal and skewer America today, as “Borat” did to the America of the 2000s, the film mostly misses its mark.

	But that’s not its intent. Sacha Baron Cohen has stated, in interviews and in a lofty cover essay in Time magazine, that the real reason he wanted to bring Ali G back is precisely because the character is now so dated and “problematic.” Between innocuous guerrilla bits, “Who Iz I?” really is about Ali G. He shows up in his bling, with his dreds tucked under a rastacap, and the movie proceeds to deconstruct what a relic he is (he has a testy back and forth with a DEI counselor), goofing on his attitudes even as it’s milking them for cheap laughs.

	It also introduces Ali G’s foil, a professor named Dr. Nira Cain-N’Degeocello, also played by Baron Cohen, buried under latex prosthetics and a costume that turns him into a 70ish left-wing boomer (balding pate and ponytail, arrogant bullfrog jowls, wire-framed glasses, patterned sweaters), with a whiny voice of voracious high-mindedness. He’s the film’s parody of “wokeness.” “Who Iz I?” mocks Ali G, and it also mocks the geek adversary who will do anything to shut him down. The movie is trying to be an equal-opportunity drive-by farce for the age of toxic extremes. At one point, as Ali puts it, “Me was cancelized.”
	

	But here’s the problem. By turning Ali G into the doofus antihero of his own absurdist saga, “Who Iz I?” becomes Sacha Baron Cohen’s version of a “Saturday Night Live” movie, like “MacGruber” or “Stuart Saves His Family” or “A Night at the Roxbury.” The film has a few scattered giggles, but it’s dawdling and cumbersome, and far less “relevant” than it thinks. For a brief spell, Ali falls under the delusion that he’s the biological son of A$AP Rocky, and this makes for comedy that’s both intentionally and unintentionally cringe. To prove that Ali is white, the professor needs a DNA sample, and the sequence in which he gets it plays to the yahoo peanut gallery.

	Ali G and Julie, flat broke, have arrived in L.A. because Ali thinks he can revive his talk-show series that ran for two seasons on HBO. (It ended in 2004.) When it turns out that he can’t, he falls into the grip of a right-wing network that’s willing to feature him as the host of “The Free Speech Show.” There’s fascist banter and Elon Musk stiff-arm salutes. Baron Cohen also plays Col. Erran Morad, the former Mossad agent who speaks in a thick Israeli accent (he’s the least funny of the three characters). Morad spearheads the kidnapping of Julie, who gives birth in a scene of gonzo fakery, with the militia men acting as obstetricians.

	Even in my days of Ali G fanhood, when I found him to be a delectable idiot, he was most funny as a talk-show stooge. It’s not as if I wanted to know his backstory or watch him go through the motions of an ersatz rescue thriller. But “Ali G: Who Iz I?” lays on that stuff, because the film is so busy working to justify its existence that it makes the mistake of pretending that Ali G “matters.”

schema.headline: ‘Ali G: Who Iz I?’ Review: Sacha Baron Cohen Brings Back His Cretinous Fake OG Talk-Show Host, Only Now Ali G Is the Film’s ‘Political’ Subject. A Mistake, Innit?

title: Kacey Musgraves to Release New 16-Song Album, ‘Middle of Nowhere Vol. 2: Tex Mex Tapes’
description: Kacey Musgraves will release a 16-song album of all-new material titled “Middle of Nowhere Vol. 2: Tex Mex Tapes” on January 15, 2027 via Lost High
body:
Kacey Musgraves will release a 16-song album of all-new material titled “Middle of Nowhere Vol. 2: Tex Mex Tapes” on January 15, 2027 via Lost Highway Records — just eight months after the release of Vol. 1. 

	According to the announcement, the album picks up where Vol. 1 left off, “expanding on themes of solitude, contentment, and finding beauty in the in-between.” Four of the album’s 16 songs are sung entirely in Spanish, including a newly-recorded Spanish version of “Uncertain, TX,” featuring Intocable.
	

	Musgraves will release two songs from the collection on Thursday night: “Weekend In Texas” and her rendition of the Norteño classic, “Mi Tesoro.”




	

	



	Musgraves is currently on her Middle of Nowhere Tour, which continues tonight at Oakland, CA’s Oakland Arena before finishing up with two sold-out nights at Seattle’s Climate Pledge Arena October 26th and 27th.

	Musgraves heads into this year’s CMA Awards with five nominations, including Album of the Year and Female Vocalist of the Year, as well as Song of the Year and Music Video of the Year for “Dry Spell”, and Musical Event of the Year for “Horses and Divorces” with Miranda Lambert. The 60th Annual CMA Awards broadcast live from Nashville’s Bridgestone Arena Wednesday, November 18 at 8/7c on ABC and Disney+.

	Middle of Nowhere Vol. 2: Tex Mex Tapes

	Track Listing:

	Pretty Horses

	Weekend In Texas

	Hard Conversations

	Denim On Denim

	Figure Out My Life

	Caballero

	The Vacation Song

	(Hey Baby) Qué Pasó?

	Uncertain, TX Feat. Intocable (Spanish version)
	

	Mi Tesoro

	Rodeo

	Tú Solo Tú (feat. Mariachi Oro De América) [Live in Mexico City]

	All My Exes (Kacey’s Version)

	Desert Eyes

	Pity Party

	Before The Next Teardrop Falls

schema.headline: Kacey Musgraves to Release New 16-Song Album, ‘Middle of Nowhere Vol. 2: Tex Mex Tapes’

title: Sam Heughan to Star With Viola Davis in Paramount+ Thriller Series ‘Ascent’
description: “Outlander” star Sam Heughan has been cast to star opposite Viola Davis in Paramount+‘s upcoming thriller “Ascent,” set in the world of global corp
body:
“Outlander” star Sam Heughan has been cast to star opposite Viola Davis in Paramount+‘s upcoming thriller “Ascent,” set in the world of global corporate crisis and damage control.

	In the series, which Davis also executive produces, Heughan will play “Conal,” described as “one of Ascent Ventures top agents. A lethally charming and natural chameleon, Conal uses social cunning and ruthlessness to get the job done, and he always gets a thrill out of completing a mission.”
	

	As previously announced, Davis is set to play “Catriona,” who according to the series logline is “an elite corporate fixer, who must weaponize the ruthless skills that have made her indispensable to billion-dollar clients when her estranged daughter is in danger.”


	Yes, there is a bit of coincidental serendipity that Heughan’s character has been paired with a “Catriona.” For eight seasons and 101 episodes of “Outlander,” Heughan starred opposite his similarly named co-star Caitriona Balfe.

	“Ascent” comes from Paramount Television Studios, and was created by John Logan (“Skyfall,” “Gladiator”). Logan is showrunner and executive producer, alongside executive producers Michael Aguilar (“Penny Dreadful: City of Angels,” “The Departed”), and Viola Davis and Julius Tennon via their JuVee Productions.

	Production on “Ascent” will kick off in Los Angeles in 2027, with an airdate on Paramount+ to be announced later.

	As part of “Outlander,” which Heughan also produced, he received award nominations including BAFTA Scotland and Critics’ Choice. His other TV credits include “The Couple Next Door,” “Men in Kilts: A Road Trip with Sam and Graham” and the upcoming “Embassy” with J.K. Simmons and Anna Kendrick. In film, he was seen in “Love Again,” “The Spy Who Dumped Me,” “Bloodshot” and “SAS: Red Notice.”
	

	On stage, Heughan played “Macbeth” last year at the Royal Shakespeare Company; he’s also written three New York Times bestselling books. 

	Heughan is repped by United Agents, UTA, Anonymous Content and Viewpoint.

schema.headline: Sam Heughan to Star With Viola Davis in Paramount+ Thriller Series ‘Ascent’

title: The True Cost of Corporate Dominance in the Music Industry (Guest Post)
description: Rev. Moose is founder of Marauder, which helps companies, organizations, and government entities develop strategies and in-person events that drive
body:
Rev. Moose is founder of Marauder, which helps companies, organizations, and government entities develop strategies and in-person events that drive change and foster growth within the independent music sector. An industry veteran with experience in artist development, marketing, advocacy, non-profit management, and international program development, he is the founding and emeritus executive director of the National Independent Venue Association (NIVA) and National Independent Venue Foundation (NIVF), as well as co-founder of the Association of Music Offices (AMO).
	

	Variety welcomes responsible commentary, please email music@variety.com if interested. 


	With Halloween nigh, the music industry might heed some warnings from horror films. As the lore goes, vampires are only allowed to enter a home once invited in.

	This is exactly what we’ve done by permitting massive corporations to dominate what could otherwise be a competitive, independent music industry. Decades ago, independent powerhouse labels like Atlantic and Virgin called their own shots; today those same companies along with the vast majority of their peers fall under only three umbrella companies. Seemingly indomitable, these conglomerates lease out their proprietary distribution channels to independent artists and labels, feeding even more life to the gluttonous monster under the bed. What isn’t outright owned, is still dominated by these same forces, regardless of opposition.

	Fear isn’t just a movie trope; it’s a controlling force of the music business. With market consolidation being what it is, taking a vocal stand is likely to echo through empty halls. All of the major artists that withdrew their music from Spotify over Joe Rogan’s misinformation campaign in the post-COVID years are back on the platform; Spotify showed no meaningful adverse effect from the calls-to-action. The band Lawrence, who testified in front of the U.S. Senate Judiciary Committee about Live Nation’s monopolistic practices, announced a tour exactly one year later largely promoted and hosted across Live Nation and Ticketmaster venues… not that they had a choice if they hoped to perform in rooms of a certain size. 
	

	Collaborating with these huge multinationals is accepted as a necessary evil in order to make it in this business. As Ellie Goulding’s lawsuit against her former management demonstrates, the argument that working with one sector of a conglomerate means the rest of the machine will be leveraged in an artist’s favor is outdated. The more power conceded, the fewer options an artist has in the future to make independent choices of who to work with and under what terms.

	This gradual consumption of the marketplace is how we ended up with an indefensibly small number of companies controlling every major sector of the music business: touring, recording, publishing, media, distribution, management and more. Most of these companies have heavily overlapping interests. This leaves multiple, conflicting revenue streams in the hands of a few decision makers that only have their own interests in mind (oh, and the closing price of their stock).

	It’s harmful to our communities that a handful of companies control the very mechanisms for art to reach an audience. In my TEDx Talk, “All Music Is Local,” I said that artists have little say over working with these massive corporations if they want their music to be seen, heard, or paid for. It’s not that independent options don’t exist; numerous independent record labels, managers, agents, publishers, distributors, venues, promoters, and media outlets show up every single day. Yet how visible can an artist realistically be without getting into business with one of these core gatekeepers?

	In the fright flick that is today’s music industry, many independents are running through the woods just trying to survive while the publicly traded behemoths lumber behind with brute force and a steady gait. Quarterly reports bragging about job creation and economic impact have no mention of the local, independently owned businesses squeezed out to make room for them, or the voices actually from local communities silenced by default for not fitting a globally marketable ideal.

	While Live Nation claims billions upon billions of dollars in earnings, nearly two-thirds of independent venue operators lose money just to stay open. Is one company really that much better at operating a business, as they claim to be, than thousands of others, or is the market intentionally skewed in their favor? Live Nation’s recent claim touting positive economic impact in local communities was refuted by a report showing taxpayers have been subsidizing one company at the expense of locally owned and operated businesses. None of this even mentions the silencing of cultures within these communities, with origin stories being thwarted due to a lack of local representation.
	

	The music industry has been and continues to be taken over by a small number of companies whose only goal is complete and total dominance. The entire independent music community as well as the European Union rallied against Universal Music Group’s acquisition of Downtown for a reason. What’s more terrifying is that the age-old path toward an independent success story seems out of reach, at least not without major financial backers. Bandcamp, a platform founded on artistic control, should have been the case model for financial independence. Instead, it was sold off to a gaming company then staff drastically reduced by the next owners. Here we are, yet again bemoaning a company once built on audiences and ideals.

	Change starts by making conscious decisions with which partners we work, which platforms are kept viable by our advertising dollars, how we prioritize ownership structure in our teams, where we provide access, and, ultimately, who benefits when fans buy tickets or enjoy music. This isn’t just idealism, these are very real steps we can each take the next time we’re reviewing a tour routing, or ad buy, or deciding which contract to sign. To be clear, this is not about passing judgment on those working with massive corporations; when there is only one show in town (often, quite literally), compromise is coercion, not submission.

	Things won’t change overnight. Systemic shifts start with intentional moves, just like you would check a child’s candy trove for razor blades. Or, to quote “Night of the Living Dead,” the most terrifying film ever made, “They’re coming to get you, Barbara.” And we all know how that ended for Barbara.

schema.headline: The True Cost of Corporate Dominance in the Music Industry (Guest Post)

title: Trump Says Google CEO Rejected His Request to Rename Atlantic Ocean on Google Maps
description: President Donald Trump, who has already renamed two bodies of water after America, said he would like to redub the Atlantic Ocean as well — but tha
body:
President Donald Trump, who has already renamed two bodies of water after America, said he would like to redub the Atlantic Ocean as well — but that the CEO of Google pushed back on the idea.

	At a rally at Clemson University in South Carolina Tuesday evening, Trump told the crowd, “So we have a lake. And we have a gulf. Now we need a river, and we need an ocean.” Trump continued: “I only like two oceans: the Atlantic Ocean and the Pacific Ocean. I’m not gonna put either ‘Trump’ or ‘America’ on any other ocean but these two.”
	

	Last year, Trump declared that the Gulf of Mexico would henceforth be known as the “Gulf of America.” Then this August, amid a trade feud with Canada, he ordered Lake Ontario to be now called “Lake America.”


	Trump said he “seriously looked at” renaming the Atlantic Ocean and called Sundar Pichai, CEO of Alphabet and Google, to ask about whether Google Maps would rename the Atlantic.

	“I said, ‘Sundar, I’m thinking of the Atlantic Ocean. Can you handle it?'” Trump recalled. According to Trump, the Google CEO responded, “No, no, no — this time I’m not doing it… Oceans are different, sir. They cover really a lot of countries. Please don’t ask us to do that.”

	Trump said after the conversation with Pichai, he would “probably pass” on trying to rename the Atlantic Ocean.

	Reps for Google did not respond to a request for comment.

	In the U.S., Google Maps displays both the Gulf of Mexico and Lake Ontario with the new Trump-designated monikers but includes the more recognizable names in parentheses in search results.

schema.headline: Trump Says Google CEO Rejected His Request to Rename Atlantic Ocean on Google Maps

title: FIFA Opens Bids for 2030 World Cup U.S. Media Rights — With Option For 2034
description:
The next FIFA World Cup is years away — but one game is already afoot.

	The international governing body behind the popular global tournament is o
body:
The next FIFA World Cup is years away — but one game is already afoot.

	The international governing body behind the popular global tournament is opening the bidding process for rights to the event for 2030 in the U.S. and Puerto Rico, and will offer an option for interesting parties to also try and secure rights for the 2034 championship as well, says Romy Gai, the group’s chief business officer, during a recent interview.


	“The idea is to be extremely flexible, the executive tells Variety, in order to “try to get the best momentum after the great success we had during World Cup 2026.” Proposals are due by noon on November 19.
	

	Fox is estimated to have paid $485 million for its World Cup rights, while NBCU is estimated to have paid $600 million for Telemundo‘s. A FIFA spokesman declined to comment on the value of previous rights fees, but Gai said the organization expected to secure more in the next round of negotiations, owing to the growing value of sports to media companies and the fact that the rights have not come up for bid in a decade and a half. Fox Sports and Telemundo telecast the event in 2018, 2022 and 2024.

	Streamers “can deliver a bigger opportunity to get in touch with new audiences,” he says. “We want to be open and flexible, to hear what they need. Ultimately, the scope is to engage more and deeper with our fans around the world.”

	The bidding is likely to attract a host of both old-school and new-tech media companies, all eager to secure the massive crowds that advertisers continue to covet. In the streaming era, audiences that watch programming simultaneously have become very difficult to generate. Most viewers cobble together their own schedules of comedies, dramas, reality shows, movie and sports, toggling between sundry streaming services that range from HBO Max to Netflix to Fox One to Disney+. But Madison Avenue can’t make cash registers ring by targeting small groups of consumers streaming a repeat of “Mad Men” during primetime hours.
	

	The most recent World Cup, which took place across the United States, was a ratings and ad-revenue bonanza for both Fox Corp. and Comcast, generating hundreds of millions in cash from advertising. While the Super Bowl is the media-industry’s biggest annual event, the World Cup, with its weeks of game play and ability to attract audiences around the globe, is a behemoth that cannot be ignored. 

	Interest in the tournament has given rise to large groups watching games in bars and friends’ homes, creating “more of a socio-cultural event than probably anyone could have imagined in their wildest dreams,” Fox Sports CEO and Executive Producer Eric Shanks told Variety earlier this year. FIFA says that over 39 days and 104 matches, the tournament averaged 13.5 million viewers per match on linear and streaming platforms, up 166% from the 2022 tournament in Qatar. Every U.S. men’s national team match drew more than 20 million viewers, while the Final attracted an average of 63 million, making it the most-watched soccer match in US history.

	Comcast, owner of NBCU and Telemundo said Thursday that World Cup telecasts boosted the media operation’s overall U.S. ad revenue by 14.6% during the third quarter. Without the games, U.S. ad revenue would have increased a mere 0.3%.

	FIFA will consider doing separate deals for linear and streaming, Gai says, but also packages that include both platforms. FIFA is open to a single company handling all aspects of a World Cup plan, but also to joint bids, he adds. FIFA’s preference, he says, is to keep Spanish-language and English-language rights under the same umbrella, but even that condition “is not mandatory.” Netflix recently secured U.S. rights to the 2027 and 2031 Women’s World Cup and will telecast in both English and Spanish.

	“I expect, honestly, a multitude of very different possibilities we can then sit down and discuss,” says Gai. FIFA in a statement says it will look for “the entity, or entities, best placed to deliver comprehensive, high-quality coverage in the United States and Puerto Rico, reach large audiences through innovative ways to watch, and contribute revenues for the benefit of football.”

	The FIFA World Cup 2030 will be hosted in Morocco, Portugal and Spain, with three centenary celebration matches in Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay marking 100 years since the first FIFA World Cup was played in 1930. Saudi Arabia will stage the FIFA World Cup 2034. This could raise a sticking point in negotiations, as U.S. companies might worry that games not in U.S. time zones will generate smaller audiences.
	

	Which companies will want to bid? Netflix already has the rights to stream the 2030 World Cup in Spain and Angorra.

schema.headline: FIFA Opens Bids for 2030 World Cup U.S. Media Rights — With Option For 2034

title: ‘Dispatch’ Developer Sets Live Concert Event to Celebrate Hit Indie Game’s One-Year Anniversary, With 5 Million Players (EXCLUSIVE)
description: It’s been one year since indie game developer AdHoc Studio launched its now-hit episodic narrative superhero adventure game “Dispatch” — and in tha
body:
It’s been one year since indie game developer AdHoc Studio launched its now-hit episodic narrative superhero adventure game “Dispatch” — and in that time the game has  attracted more than 5 million players. Now, the team behind the title (which has doubled in size since last October) has decided to celebrate its digital win in the physical world.

	Titled “Dispatch: Night Shift,” the anniversary event is described as “an in-person, live entertainment experience.” Set up by AdHoc as a one-night exclusive show taking place in December in Los Angeles, Night Shift will bring the game’s songs and its original score together on one stage with the score acting as the connection between each set, just as it connects the game.
	

	Among those set to take the stage at the live event are “Dispatch” composer Andrew Arcadi, who will perform the game’s original score live alongside select artists who contributed to the game’s soundtrack, including Thot Squad, Bershy, Primer, Caroline Kingsbury and Fartbarf, playing tracks from “Dispatch” and their own albums.


	The “Dispatch: Night Shift” event will be held at the Avalon Hollywood nightclub in Los Angeles on Dec. 3. Doors will open at 6 p.m. and the Night Shift show will kick off at 7 p.m. Because tickets are “extremely limited,” fans are encouraged to sign up for AdHoc Studio’s email list to access ticket sales early at this link. Pre-sale tickets go live on Oct. 28 with purchases limited to two tickets per person; more info is available at this link.

	Along with the live show, AdHoc is marking “Dispatch’s” one-year birthday with a number other surprises. That includes a free update to the Deluxe Edition featuring two new behind-the-scenes modes: Commentary and Storyboard. Commentary Mode features more than 16 hours of cast and crew commentary, and Storyboard Mode lets players experience the entire game through the original storyboard animatics. Existing Deluxe Edition owners will have access to Commentary Mode and Storyboard Mode with a free update, while Standard Edition owners can purchase the Deluxe upgrade for $10.99.
	

	The company also announced that “Dispatch” is coming to mobile: The game will launch on Android and iOS, with support for Google Play Games on PC, starting Dec. 9, 2026. The mobile release includes the base game, rebuilt for touch and vertical play. At launch, players will be able to access the first four episodes for free and unlock the full mobile release for $19.99.

	In addition, AdHoc announced a lineup of “Dispatch” anniversary merch, featuring artwork by the game’s art director, Derek Stratton. Created for the Dispatch three-record soundtrack vinyl set available exclusively through Lost In Cult, the designs can now be found on shirts and hoodies. In addition, 100 album-art posters signed by Stratton will be available for purchase. AdHoc and Lost In Cult also are expanding their collaboration with a “Dispatch: Design Works” collection, featuring a hardcover book and collectible box featuring interviews from the cast, developers and more.

	Aaron Paul stars in “Dispatch” as the voice of Robert Robertson, a.k.a. Mecha Man, who is at the center of a dysfunctional team of misfit heroes. You play as dispatch operator Robert, who must strategize about who to send to emergencies around the city, all while balancing office politics, personal relationships, and his own quest to become a hero with a damaged suit. The game’s cast includes Laura Bailey (“The Last of Us Part II,” Critical Role), Erin Yvette (“Hades II,” “The Wolf Among Us”) and Jeffrey Wright (“American Fiction,” “The Batman”).

	AdHoc chief operating officer Nick Herman and CEO Michael Choung, two of the studio’s founders, say the concert-style “Dispatch: Night Shift” experience has been in the works since January. At that time, several of the musicians who participated in the “Dispatch” soundtrack were asking if they could include assets from the game in their own live performances.



	

	



	“It felt like there was an opportunity here where we have our fans going to their shows. Why don’t we create a place for everyone and have basically like a mini-festival and celebrate all this stuff,” Herman says. “As soon as we had the idea, it was like, ‘OK, this is gonna be overproduced, we’re gonna go crazy.’ We’ve never produced a concert, so we’re working with Banter Events who has experience doing live events and they’ve been really great at teaching us how to do this. It’s kind of similar to ‘Dispatch’ where we had never made a premium animated television show through that pipeline. It’s kind of nice not knowing because then you just ask for crazy stuff, and then they go, OK, and then we’ll figure it out.”
	

	Herman has had “Night Shift” “written in the top corner in permanent marker” for the team since the beginning of the year, when the game was coming off the high of impressive early sales and multiple 2025 Game Awards nominations.

	“There certainly was a plan — but I will say, the energy, especially in January, was more drunk than sober in the sense that the success just walloped all of us,” Choung says. “We had no idea what that was, it was just like, we got to do something. And then Nick was like, let’s do this. We signed up for it knowing nothing about how to do this stuff.”

	Herman says that the launch of “Dispatch” has “given us confidence in our instincts.”

	“This is our first original as a studio, the first original IP that we’ve ever done as as creatives,” says Herman. “So whenever there’s a weird idea, we’re like, ‘Well, maybe it’s not so weird, the last weird idea works.’ We’re really excited and bullish on the future of what we’re doing and what our teams are building.”

	Adds Choung, “I think one of the things that success has meant for us, which is again entirely new, is a blank page. And that’s kind of both a benefit and a curse for a writer. It’s like the best thing you can hand someone. It’s the worst thing you can hand someone. And so we’re filling it in with things that we just never thought we could do. We’re also not in a crazy rush to fill it out, because the potential and the possibilities of a blank page are so exciting. So there’s a lot of ideas and a lot of thoughts inside of the studio about what could be next, what we ought to be doing.”

schema.headline: ‘Dispatch’ Developer Sets Live Concert Event to Celebrate Hit Indie Game’s One-Year Anniversary, With 5 Million Players (EXCLUSIVE)

                          I'm Dog-Tired of These Legal Proceedings!!!
body:
Clavicular
                          I'm Dog-Tired of These Legal Proceedings!!!
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              October 22, 2026
                            8:13 AM PDT
                                                                      |

                                  October 22, 2026
                                9:13 AM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Clavicular's courtroom entourage apparently includes man's best friend ... because he was walking a dog on his way into a major hearing in his rape case.
      
    
            The streamer was spotted walking from the parking lot to the Orleans District Court in Massachusetts on Thursday with a white dog on a leash.
      
    
            The dog seemed unhappy about all the attention Clav was getting ... barking at a crowd of onlookers who were filming them.
      

            Sources familiar with the situation tell TMZ ... the dog is named Morris -- and Clavicular's team rescued him from Agora Hills Animal Shelter several months ago.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            We're told Morris refused to leave Clav's side this morning ... so he brought the dog with him. Our sources say this was a last-second decision.
      
    
            While Morris looks frustrated in one of these pics, our sources say the dog is actually very friendly and barely barks ... but it seems the press attention set him off.
      
    
            We've also learned Morris wasn't allowed into the courtroom ... but one of Clav's team did take him to a nearby Starbucks for a pup cup. 
      
    
            Clavicular was arraigned on one count of rape, one count of drugging someone for sexual intercourse, and one count of procuring liquor for someone under 21 years old in connection with an alleged 2025 incident. He pled not guilty to all charges.
      
    
            He was ultimately released on $10,000 bail ... though he's been told to stay away from the alleged victim and not to post about her again on social media. The judge also ordered him to turn in his passport.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            As we reported ... Clavicular was charged last month after a woman claimed he had sex with her when she was too inebriated to consent.
      
    
            He has vehemently denied all her allegations -- and has even shared alleged messages which he claims refute her allegations.

title: Rep. Ilhan Omar Responds to Claims Ex-Husband Is Her Brother
description:
Rep. Ilhan Omar
                          Asked If Ex-Husband Is Her Brother ...
body:
Rep. Ilhan Omar
                          Asked If Ex-Husband Is Her Brother ...
                          'Not to My Knowledge'
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              October 21, 2026
                            7:57 PM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  October 22, 2026
                                8:56 AM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Ilhan Omar is addressing the longstanding allegation she married her brother to commit immigration fraud.
      
    
            During an interview with MS NOW's Chris Hayes, the Minnesota congresswoman was asked whether her former husband, Ahmed Nur Said Elmi, is actually her brother, responding, "Not to my knowledge."
      
    
            Omar also called the allegations "insane," pushing back against claims surrounding her 2009 marriage to Elmi. The allegations have circulated for years, though no evidence has publicly established that Elmi is her brother.
      

            The interview comes after federal agents raided Omar's Washington, D.C., home on October 12 as part of an ongoing criminal investigation.
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            Trump has denied involvement in the raid, while the Justice Department says agents executed a judicially authorized search warrant.
      
    
            According to Reuters, investigators are examining whether Omar or members of her family made false statements in immigration paperwork dating back decades.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Omar has denied wrongdoing and accused President Donald Trump's administration of using the investigation to intimidate her ahead of the midterm elections.
